Subject: Capacity vs feature credits — help selecting plan

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Clearwell is excited to move a small pilot (6 months) across our search and triage workflows. Before we lock a trial, we need pragmatic guidance on how to pick the right entry plan. Two things we care about: predictable token/unit economics for bursty traffic and access to the advanced reranking/reroute features your team showed.

High-level numbers: baseline 200 concurrent queries/day, but we have a few internal pipelines that can produce short bursts up to ~6k q/day for 1–3 hours, roughly 3–4x on peak days. We expect mostly short sequences (avg 150 tokens) but occasional multi-turn sessions that hit KV cache pressure.

Questions:
- Would you recommend taking the higher-capacity tier up front or buying a lower base + feature credits for reranking and routing?
- What is the downgrade path if the pilot doesn't sustain? Any pro‑rata for unused committed capacity?
- Are there bundling discounts if we commit to a 12‑month term for the pilot after a successful 6‑month test?

Attaching a short requirements doc. Can we jump on a 30‑min call next week to map options?

Thanks,
Samira Qureshi
Head of ML

Hi Samira — great to hear and thanks for the details + attachment. I pulled together a short recommendation after reviewing your burst profile. TL;DR: recommend a hybrid approach for the pilot — reserve a modest baseline capacity and add a bucket of feature credits for reranking/advanced routing.

Rationale:
- Baseline reserve (Medium tier): covers day-to-day latency targets and preserves KV caching benefits so multi-turn sessions stay warm.
- Feature credits: let you enable expensive features (reranking, multi-model routing) only when needed during bursts; cheaper than permanently moving to the next higher tier if bursts are infrequent.

Tradeoffs & notes:
- Upside of higher-tier: lower per-token cost at scale and simpler billing, but you pay for unused guaranteed capacity during quiet periods.
- Downside of credits-only: potential higher per-token cost when credits run out; you'll need automated fallback policies to avoid latency cliffs.

Downgrade / billing path:
- We support month-to-month downgrades for hosted plans with a 30‑day notice. Commit discounts (12 months) are applied up front and are non‑prorated; however, for pilot customers we can offer a partial credit ladder: if you commit to 12 months after the 6‑month pilot we can credit up to 40% of pilot paid fees toward the annual commit (details in attached proposal).

Suggested next steps:
1) I attached a draft proposal (clearwell-proposal-v1.xlsx) and our discount matrix for reference.
2) If this aligns, we propose: Medium tier baseline + 50k feature credits, 6‑month pilot, option to convert to 12‑month with a 12% commit discount and up to 40% pilot credit.
3) Book a 30‑min call so Marcus/Laura can walk pricing and SLAs.

Would next Tuesday 10–10:30 PT work?

Best,

We should avoid a big upfront discount for a 6‑month pilot. Options I like:

Operational note: ensure billing flags are set so feature credits auto-apply to reranking routes and do not leak into lower-priority tiers. Laura, can you confirm we can earmark credits to the routed flows?
